name: Uterine Cervical Aplasia and Agenesis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Cervical Agenesis

criteria.description: Complete absence of the cervical canal confirmed by imaging
Primary amenorrhea despite normal secondary sexual characteristics
Presence of a normally developed uterine body without cervical tissue

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of primary amenorrhea with imaging-confirmed absence of the cervical canal
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by pelvic MRI or ultrasound imaging.

pathognomonic.notes: Absence of menstruation despite normal secondary sexual development

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absence of cervical canal on imaging
searchTerms: absence of cervical opening seen on scan
no visible cervical passage on ultrasound

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cyclic pelvic pain due to hematometra
pathognomonic.notes: Pain caused by menstrual blood accumulation in uterus
searchTerms: cyclic lower belly pain from blood buildup
periodic pelvic cramping due to trapped menstrual blood

common.notes: Normal breast development and pubic hair
Palpable mass from retained menstrual blood
searchTerms: pelvic swelling caused by trapped blood
pelvic mass due to menstrual blood accumulation

common.notes: Inability to conceive due to cervical absence

occasional.notes: Associated renal malformations such as unilateral renal agenesis
Painful intercourse due to vaginal hypoplasia
Ectopic endometrial tissue due to obstructed outflow

searchTerms: psychological issues related to inability to conceive

rare.notes: Rarely observed vertebral or limb malformations

laboratory: Normal hormonal profile including FSH, LH, estrogen
imaging: Pelvic MRI showing absence of cervical canal
Ultrasound demonstrating normal uterine body with hematometra
Renal ultrasound to assess for urinary tract anomalies
genetic: No specific gene identified; sporadic congenital malformation
other: Diagnostic laparoscopy may reveal hematometra and endometriosis

distinguishingFeatures: Complete absence of uterus and upper two-thirds of vagina
No uterine body present on imaging
Obstruction at vaginal level causing hematocolpos

redFlags: Primary amenorrhea with cyclic pelvic pain
Urinary tract anomalies associated with reproductive tract malformations
references: Acién P. Cervical agenesis: diagnosis and management. Fertil Steril. 2011;95(6):2157-2160.
Rock JA, Zacur HA. Congenital absence of the cervix: clinical features and management. Obstet Gynecol. 1989;74(5):715-718.
Orphanet: Uterine cervical aplasia and agenesis (ORPHA:180145)
